baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated zani/zaniya nouns, reciprocal yankiḥu clauses, two illa restrictions, and final ḥurrima clause.
baseline_models.mechanism: Known zina supplies the conduct class, nikah as marriage contract supplies the regulated bond, and ḥ-r-m as prohibition converts the gender-reciprocal syntax into a rule for the believing community rather than a one-way observation.

activation_trace.role: Known zina supplies the repeated male and female conduct category.
Marriage contract and marrying supply the juridical relation restricted by each illa.
Association with God supplies the explicitly confessional alternative in both gendered halves.
Prohibition and prevention make the closing clause normatively operative.
Heart-settled assent supplies the identity of the community bound by the rule.

changed_reading.before: A one-directional report about the kind of woman a male offender happens to marry.
changed_reading.after: A reciprocal rule governing whom the named male and female classes may marry and barring that relation to believers.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Both occurrences of yankiḥu can activate intercourse, while sh-r-k can activate participation and ḥ-r-m can activate inviolable right.
baseline_models.mechanism: Nikah as intercourse keeps the focus on sexual access as well as formal marriage. Shirk as participation then makes both alternatives forms of shared boundary breach, while the closing ḥurma protects believers from entering that participation.

activation_trace.role: Known zina anchors the model in illicit sexual conduct.
Intercourse supplies a sexual-access reading alongside the contractual one.
Participation between parties supplies the shared-involvement structure without replacing the explicit mushrik label.
Inviolable right and protected bond make the closing ban a defense of communal sexual integrity.
Security and trust supply the protected condition endangered by illicit participation.

changed_reading.before: The verse regulates only eligibility for a marriage contract.
changed_reading.after: It can also regulate sexual access and shared participation in illicit conduct, with believers kept outside that relation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Nikah and shirk each carry an affinity or marital-association branch, and the prohibition is placed specifically upon believers.
baseline_models.mechanism: The affinal-membership branch of n-k-h and the affinity branch of sh-r-k expose a shared relational structure: a spouse is incorporated into a network of kinship and trust. Without erasing the ordinary zina and polytheism senses, the verse can therefore guard communal incorporation, not merely a private act.

activation_trace.role: Known zina remains the conduct anchor that makes incorporation problematic.
Becoming a spouse or affine supplies incorporation into a marital network.
Marital affinity supplies a relational echo inside the mushrik alternative, secondary to its ordinary doctrinal sense.
Protected right, compact, and inviolability supply the boundary around incorporation.
Trust and security supply the social condition the boundary preserves.

changed_reading.before: The verse bans an isolated private pairing.
changed_reading.after: It may also bar an incompatible person-status from affinal incorporation into a trust-bearing believing network.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah opens by declaring itself imposed and its signs clarifying. That opening activates the focus ḥurrima as a delimited prescription, sharply weakening a merely statistical reading of who tends to pair with whom.

activation_trace.role: Prohibition supplies the focus rule whose modality is being sharpened.
A specified binding obligation supplies the surah-level prescriptive frame.
Clarification by speech or sign supplies an announced disclosure frame for the rule.

structural_cues: 24:1 precedes the sanction and pairing clauses with a surah-level declaration of imposition and clarification.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an imposed-surah frame and the focus supplies ḥurrima; I infer that the frame governs the focus clause. A live alternative is that the first two clauses still state a social regularity before the final prohibition.

changed_reading.before: The reciprocal clauses chiefly predict an offender's actual partner.
changed_reading.after: They sit inside an announced prescriptive unit, with the final prohibition controlling the practical force.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same zina labels enter a witnessed sanction, while later speech-throwing and knowledge-based testimony rules distinguish an accusation from an established status. The focus categories therefore cannot be assigned by rumor merely to trigger its exclusion.

activation_trace.role: Known zina anchors the labels whose evidentiary status is at issue.
The same known-zina nouns place the labels in an immediately adjacent sanction context.
Presence with observation supplies the public-witness setting of the sanction.
Casting words at another supplies the mechanism of accusation distinct from proved conduct.
Knowledge-based declaration supplies the proof threshold and the regulated status of testimony.

structural_cues: 24:2 repeats the paired zani/zaniya nouns immediately before the focus and places their sanction before a witnessing group.
24:4-13 repeatedly separates charge, witness, oath, truth, and lie; 24:11-19 then condemns ungrounded circulation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated labels, public witnessing, speech-casting, and proof rules; I infer that applying the focus labels is proof-governed. A live alternative is that 24:3 describes a moral type even when no court process occurs.

changed_reading.before: Anyone suspected or spoken of as sexually immoral can be treated as a zani or zaniya for the focus restriction.
changed_reading.after: The restriction operates in an evidentiary field: accusation and social repetition do not by themselves establish its person-status.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediate repair and forgiveness vocabulary, then repeated forgiveness across the surah, weakens a reading in which the focus participles are irreversible essences. The focus still states a real prohibition, but the whole-surah field makes present actionable status more plausible than permanent ontology.

activation_trace.role: Known zina supplies the conduct-derived person label whose duration is questioned.
Prohibition supplies the real boundary that need not imply an immutable identity.
Repair opposed to corruption supplies a route by which a sanctioned status can change.
Covering sin and shielding its bearer from its effect supplies non-permanence of consequence.

structural_cues: 24:5 places an exception of return and repair directly after a penalty provision.
Forgiveness and mercy recur at 24:10, 24:20, 24:22, 24:26, 24:33, and 24:62.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repair and repeated shielding from sin's effects; I infer that conduct labels need not be lifelong essences. A live alternative is that 24:5 repairs only the false accuser's status and leaves the exact effect on 24:3 unstated.

changed_reading.before: Zani and zaniya denote fixed identities and the restriction is necessarily lifelong.
changed_reading.after: They can denote current conduct-linked status; the surah makes restoration live while leaving its exact timing and procedure unresolved.

context_deltas.mechanism: The fourfold khabith/tayyib chiasm formally echoes the focus's gender-reciprocal syntax. Corrupt mixing and a marriage-bearing tayyib branch activate compatibility, but acquittal from what people say blocks the reverse inference from association or speech to guilt.

activation_trace.role: Marriage supplies the focus relation whose reciprocal formula is being compared.
Participation supplies the focus's association structure without displacing doctrinal shirk.
Corruption through mixing with corrupt people supplies the negative compatibility pattern.
The branch joining goodness with food and marriage makes marital scope live in the positive reciprocal formula.
Acquittal and separation supply a firewall between persons and allegations.
Saying or attributing what did not occur identifies false attribution as the relation from which they are cleared.

structural_cues: 24:26 repeats four gender-marked type terms in an A-for-A, A-for-A pattern resembling 24:3.
The verse closes by clearing its subjects from what others say, inside the long accusation sequence of 24:11-25.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the formal echo, mixing and marriage branches, and explicit acquittal from sayings; I infer that the echo constrains how 24:3 may be socially used. A live alternative is that 24:26 classifies speech and speakers independently of marriage.

changed_reading.before: An observed spouse or associate can be used backward to prove that a person belongs to the focus's offender class.
changed_reading.after: The reciprocal formula marks normative compatibility or association, but the surah's acquittal logic blocks guilt by spouse, association, or repeated saying alone.

context_deltas.mechanism: House entry requires authorization, bodily openings require guarding, and the focus ḥ-r-m carries sanctuary and inviolability branches. Together they recast nikah as crossing a guarded intimate and household threshold rather than exercising entitlement over another person.

activation_trace.role: Affinal membership supplies entry into a spouse and household network.
A protected spatial sanctuary supplies the focus boundary's threshold image.
Inviolable right and compact supply the protected interest at that threshold.
Entry into an interior supplies the concrete threshold mechanism.
Permission and authorization supply the condition for crossing a protected threshold.
Guarding sanctity, covenant, and chastity supplies active maintenance of intimate boundaries.
The bodily opening and sexual organ supply the intimate object being guarded.

structural_cues: 24:27-29 regulates entry to houses, and 24:58-62 repeats permission at domestic and communal thresholds.
24:30-31 pairs male and female commands to lower sight and guard sexual openings before 24:32-33 addresses nikah.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated permission thresholds and bodily guarding; I infer a structural homology with marital and sexual access in 24:3. A live alternative is that house-entry rules are adjacent but independent regulations.

changed_reading.before: The focus merely lists disfavored partner categories.
changed_reading.after: It also functions within a surah-wide architecture of authorized access, protecting intimate and household incorporation as an inviolable threshold.

context_deltas.mechanism: The community must facilitate marriage, those without it must restrain themselves, and coercion into sexual commerce is prohibited where chastity is desired. This makes 24:3 a boundary within a constructive, noncoercive sexual order, not an instruction to force stigmatized classes into one another.

activation_trace.role: Marriage contract supplies the focus's regulated lawful bond.
Causing marriage for others supplies the community's positive duty to facilitate a lawful bond.
Available marriage contract supplies the lawful channel whose absence calls for restraint.
Refraining from what is improper supplies self-restraint while that channel is unavailable.
Forcing another into what she rejects supplies the prohibited coercive mechanism.
The sexual-prostitution branch, specifically activated by the bagha occurrence, supplies the exploitative alternative to nikah.
Protected sexual chastity supplies the expressed agency and boundary coercion violates.

structural_cues: 24:32 commands marriage facilitation; 24:33 moves from unavailable nikah to restraint and then bans coercion into bagha.
The focus's reciprocal wording assigns the boundary to both sexes, while the later coercion clause exposes unequal power within sexual arrangements.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a lawful channel, restraint, chastity, prostitution, and coercion; I infer that 24:3 cannot be a command to manufacture the pairings it names. A live alternative is that the focus uses nikah primarily for intercourse while 24:32-33 uses it for contract.

changed_reading.before: The community should pair a zani with a zaniya or mushrika as the verse's positive arrangement.
changed_reading.after: The verse marks a prohibited boundary; the community's positive work is to facilitate lawful marriage, require restraint, and prevent coerced sexual commerce.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later contrast between claimed belief and turning away from judgment, followed by the believers' obedient response, activates the focus's al-mu'minin as an enacted covenantal and juridical posture rather than a merely nominal demographic label.

activation_trace.role: Settled assent supplies the focus identity upon whom the prohibition rests.
Claimed assent followed by denial of the believer label supplies the nominal-versus-enacted contrast.
Turning away and refusal supply the posture that empties the verbal claim.
Judgment between people supplies the legal decision from which the nominal claimants turn.
Submission and obedience supply the believers' enacted reception of judgment.

structural_cues: 24:47 says people claim belief and obedience, then turn away, and explicitly denies that they are believers.
24:48-52 contrasts refusal of judgment with the believers' heard-and-obeyed response.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a direct contrast between nominal faith and response to judgment; I infer that the focus's believer category has practical covenantal content. A live alternative is that 24:3 addresses all professing believers regardless of later compliance.

changed_reading.before: Believers is a static residual class outside zani and mushrik.
changed_reading.after: Believer names a trust-bearing community whose identity is enacted by receiving the rule and its adjudication, not secured by profession alone.

context_deltas.mechanism: The promise sequence moves from belief to security and from worship to no shirk. That activates the juxtaposition of zina and shirk in 24:3 as an analogy between breached intimate exclusivity and breached theological exclusivity, while preserving them as distinct offenses.

activation_trace.role: Marriage contract supplies the focus's exclusive intimate covenant.
Association with God supplies the explicit theological breach placed beside zina.
Security and trust supply the communal good protected by exclusive allegiance.
The single root spanning belief and security supplies the faith-to-social-safety movement.
Submissive worship supplies the positive pole of exclusive allegiance.
Refusal to associate anything with God supplies the explicit negative pole of that allegiance.

structural_cues: 24:55 directly coordinates promised security, worship, and non-association.
24:3 alone coordinates sexual transgression, marriage or intercourse, mushrik status, prohibition, and believers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies both coordinations; I supply the analogy that each concerns exclusivity and trust. A live alternative is that 24:3 simply lists two independent prohibited classes with no shared covenant mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Mushrik is an unexplained second demographic option beside zaniya.
changed_reading.after: Mushrik marks the opposite of exclusive theological allegiance and, beside zina, creates a contained analogy between theological and intimate covenant breach.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the focus branch is a material image of rain pressing land or sleep overcoming an eye, not the ordinary legal meaning of nikah. It remains anchored in both focus occurrences and is activated by 24:33's explicit coercion and prostitution field. Downstream prose should present only a secondary pressure-and-dominance resonance, never translate yankiḥu as 'coerce' or use it to erase the contract and intercourse senses.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The two yankiḥu forms at 24:3, especially the branch in which one force bears down upon and overcomes a receptive site.

activation_trace.role: Rain pressing land or drowsiness overcoming the eye supplies a branch-distant force-over-site image.
Forcing another into what she rejects supplies the explicit dominance activator.
The sexual-prostitution branch supplies the exploitative domain in which pressure becomes morally diagnostic.

changed_reading.before: Nikah is a relation whose power dynamics remain invisible.
changed_reading.after: As a contained secondary resonance, the surah makes pressure and coercive dominance relevant to judging purported sexual or marital joining.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because road and hunter-snare branches of sh-r-k are materially distant from doctrinal mushrik. They remain anchored in both focus mushrik forms and gain a mechanism from 24:21's followed footprints leading to boundary-crossing indecency. Downstream prose should retain mushrik's doctrinal sense and render path or snare only as an exploratory account of how illicit association recruits and constrains conduct.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The repeated mushrika/mushrik alternatives, whose root inventory includes road-groove and trapping branches.

activation_trace.role: Road grooves and tracks supply an association-shaped route image.
A hunter's snare supplies the entanglement image of entering a harmful association.
Tracing one mark after another supplies the act of recruitment into a route.
Footprints followed by a traveler supply the sequential path mechanism.
Exceeding a boundary supplies the path's named moral destination.

changed_reading.before: The two excluded alternatives are static partner labels.
changed_reading.after: Secondarily, illicit association can be imagined as entry into a tracked and entangling course of conduct from which the prohibition protects believers.

strongest_changes: The surah's opening imposition and closing ḥurrima make the focus prescriptive rather than a bare prediction of spouse behavior.
Witness, accusation, and acquittal sequences make zani/zaniya proof-governed statuses and block guilt by rumor or observed association.
Household permission, bodily guarding, marriage facilitation, restraint, and the coercion ban place the focus inside an authorized and nonexploitative access order.
Later contrasts make believer an enacted response to judgment, while belief-to-security and worship-to-no-shirk sharpen the covenantal stakes.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context turned a terse reciprocal pairing formula into an intersection of adjudication, speech discipline, repair, intimate thresholds, lawful provision, anti-coercion, and exclusive trust without forcing the contract, intercourse, affinity, and exploratory material readings into one interpretation.
remaining_uncertainties: Nikah as marriage contract and nikah as intercourse both remain live in the focus syntax.
The surah activates repair but does not state within 24:3 exactly when or how repentance changes the restriction.
The 24:26 reciprocal echo may sort persons, utterances, qualities, or marital compatibility; the packet does not force one scope.
The affinity, pressure, road, and snare branches are diagnostic secondary resonances and should not replace the ordinary zina, nikah, and shirk senses.
